resources.string: Share your VPN over a hotspot or get internet from another phone
Tap to share your VPN through it

1. Enable mobile data and connect Levik to a working VPN server.
2. Turn on your phone’s Wi-Fi hotspot and protect it with a password.
3. Return here, select the hotspot address and start sharing.
4. Connect the other device to this Wi-Fi network.
No local Wi-Fi address found. Enable the hotspot, return here and refresh. Mobile and VPN addresses are not suitable.
Choose the address of your hotspot. If several addresses are shown, check the gateway in the receiving device’s Wi-Fi details. Do not choose an unrelated home or work network.
This is my password-protected hotspot. People connected to this Wi-Fi can use the manual proxy while sharing is on.
Sharing is paused. Wait for the VPN connection.
Enter the server without http:// and enter only digits in the port field. HTTPS works without installing any certificates.
Only browsers and apps that use this proxy go through Levik. Other apps, games and calls may connect directly. This mode does not protect the entire device.
Save your previous proxy settings before changing them. If a work proxy or automatic setup was configured, restore it instead of simply turning everything off.
Open this Wi-Fi network’s settings → Proxy → None, or restore the previous value. Menu names vary by Android version.
Settings → Wi-Fi → ⓘ next to this network → Configure Proxy → Off, or restore your previous settings → Save.
Settings → Network & internet → Proxy. Restore your previous manual/automatic settings. A manual proxy can remain enabled after you switch Wi-Fi networks.
System Settings → Network → Wi-Fi → Details → Proxies. Restore your previous HTTP/HTTPS and automatic settings. These settings can remain active on another Wi-Fi network.
Settings → Network → Network Proxy. Restore your previous mode and values. Check browser-specific proxy settings too, if you changed them.
Menu names vary by OS version. Samsung and Xiaomi may hide Proxy under Advanced / View more. These instructions are also available offline.

If a page does not open:
• Make sure both devices use the phone’s hotspot.
• Recheck the current server and port above: the phone’s address may change after restarting the hotspot.
• Make sure Levik on the phone is connected and sharing is ready.
• If a browser works but another app does not, that app may ignore the proxy. Use the Levik guest mode instead.
• If another Wi-Fi network stops working, restore your previous proxy settings.
Scan in Levik on the receiving device
Connect to this phone’s Wi-Fi first. In Levik choose “Get internet from a phone”, then scan this code or paste the invitation. This QR does not configure Wi-Fi.
This invitation is temporary access to your connection. Anyone with it can connect until it expires or you stop sharing. Only give it to people you trust.

1. Connect to the owner’s Wi-Fi hotspot.
2. Ask the owner to open Share VPN → With Levik.
3. Scan the QR here or paste the invitation.
4. Confirm the connection and allow the system VPN request. You do not need your own account or subscription.

The owner controls this connection. Access ends when sharing stops or expires. If the connection is lost, Levik blocks the traffic it captures while its VPN service is running. For protection after force-stopping the app, Android’s always-on VPN and “Block connections without VPN” must be enabled.
Connecting will replace the VPN currently running on this device. Saved account and server settings will be kept.
This invitation is invalid or expired. Ask the owner to start sharing again and send a new code.
Open your phone’s Settings and find Wi-Fi hotspot / Personal hotspot.
All proxy and Levik guest connections will stop. On devices using manual proxy, restore their previous settings so that other networks keep working.
Connect your own Levik VPN first. Then turn on a password-protected hotspot.

string-array.name: sharing_steps_android
string-array.item: Connect the receiving device to the phone’s Wi-Fi hotspot.
Open Settings → Network & internet → Internet. Tap the connected network’s settings icon, then Edit.
Open Advanced options → Proxy → Manual.
Copy the Server and Port shown above into Proxy hostname and Proxy port. Leave the bypass list empty.
Save the settings. Open a browser and try the page you need.
When finished, restore the previous proxy settings using the instructions below.

string-array.name: sharing_steps_samsung
string-array.item: Connect to the phone’s hotspot.
Open Settings → Connections → Wi-Fi. Tap the gear beside the connected network.
Open View more / Advanced, then Proxy → Manual. The label depends on your One UI version.
Enter the Server above as Proxy host name and the Port above as Proxy port. Leave bypass addresses empty.
Save. Open a browser and try the page you need.
When finished, set Proxy to None or restore the previous settings.

string-array.name: sharing_steps_xiaomi
string-array.item: Connect to the phone’s hotspot.
Open Settings → Wi-Fi. Tap the arrow or information icon beside the connected network.
Find Proxy (sometimes under Advanced settings) → Manual.
Enter the Server above as proxy hostname and the Port above as proxy port. Leave bypass addresses empty.
Save using the check mark / Save button. Reconnect to this Wi-Fi if necessary, then test in a browser.
When finished, set Proxy to None or restore the previous settings.

string-array.name: sharing_steps_ios
string-array.item: Connect to the phone’s hotspot in Settings → Wi-Fi.
Tap ⓘ beside that connected Wi-Fi network.
Scroll to Configure Proxy → Manual.
Enter the Server and Port shown above. Authentication stays off for this private-hotspot compatibility mode.
Tap Save. Open Safari and try the page you need.
When finished, return to Configure Proxy and restore the previous setting.

string-array.name: sharing_steps_windows
string-array.item: Connect the PC to the phone’s Wi-Fi hotspot.
Before editing, save a screenshot of your existing proxy settings, especially if you use a work proxy.
Open Settings → Network & internet → Proxy.
Under Manual proxy setup, select Set up / Edit next to Use a proxy server.
Turn it on. Enter the Server above as the IP address and the Port above. Save.
Open your browser and try the page you need. An app with its own network settings may ignore this proxy.
When finished, restore the previous manual and automatic proxy settings. Switching Wi-Fi does not necessarily turn this proxy off.

string-array.name: sharing_steps_macos
string-array.item: Connect the Mac to the phone’s hotspot.
Open Apple menu → System Settings → Network → Wi-Fi → Details → Proxies. On older macOS: System Preferences → Network → Wi-Fi → Advanced → Proxies.
Save your previous proxy settings before changing them.
Enable Web Proxy (HTTP) and Secure Web Proxy (HTTPS). Enter the same Server and Port shown above in both entries. Do not install certificates.
Confirm with OK / Apply. Open Safari and try the page you need.
When finished, restore your previous proxy settings. They can remain active after switching to another Wi-Fi network.

string-array.name: sharing_steps_linux
string-array.item: Connect to the phone’s hotspot. These steps are for GNOME; other desktops use different menus.
Save your previous proxy settings.
Open Settings → Network → Network Proxy and choose Manual.
Enter the Server and Port shown above for both HTTP and HTTPS. Leave SOCKS blank unless you already used it for another purpose.
Apply. In Firefox, choose “Use system proxy settings” if its own settings override the system. Test the page you need.
When finished, restore both the system and browser proxy settings you changed.

resources.string: The sharing action failed. Check the VPN and hotspot, then try again.
The phone’s proxy successfully opened an HTTPS test page through its configured VPN route. Now test the browser on the receiving device; this does not verify its other apps.
The proxy did not complete the HTTPS check. Check the VPN and current phone address, then try again.
Starting and stopping sharing briefly reconnects the owner’s VPN. Automatic route optimization is paused while sharing; connection recovery remains available.
